items.headline: LTA tells Grab to pause self-driving shuttle tests after a Punggol near-miss with a schoolgirl
items.summary: The Land Transport Authority has directed Grab to pause autonomous-vehicle testing at such junctions after one of its Punggol trial shuttles braked and swerved as a schoolgirl began crossing on a blinking green man on 5 November. A safety operator took manual control, and the LTA said it is reviewing whether the vehicles' response in such scenarios should be changed.

items.headline: Three firms from the 2015 haze probe are named again as a fresh haze episode hits Singapore
items.summary: The National Environment Agency told Parliament that three entities investigated over the 2015 transboundary haze have been linked to the current episode, and that their past conduct will be weighed. The disclosure came as MPs, including the WP's Eileen Chong, debated amendments that would sharply raise maximum haze fines.

items.headline: More than 112,000 people dropped private health insurance riders in 2025 as premiums rose
items.summary: Figures cited in Parliament showed that over 112,000 residents discontinued optional Integrated Shield Plan riders in 2025 after a run of premium increases. Officials said affordability is being monitored as insurers reprice their plans.

items.headline: High Court orders Singapura Heritage Food Hall wound up over an unpaid supplier debt
items.summary: The High Court ordered the operator of Singapura Heritage Food Hall to be wound up, with the order gazetted on 4 November. The winding-up followed an application by poultry supplier Toh Thye San Farm filed in September.

items.headline: Update: Delhi's air is ranked the world's most polluted on the eve of Diwali
items.summary: IQAir ranked New Delhi the world's most polluted major city on Saturday, with Friday's readings the worst pre-Diwali air in eight years. Authorities shifted schools to online classes and urged remote work as PM2.5 levels soared ahead of Sunday's festival.

items.headline: India's gold demand gets a festive boost as prices pull back before Diwali
items.summary: Crisil Ratings reported rising footfall and a higher share of shoppers converting to purchases in the October-December quarter, helped by a pullback in gold prices and the start of the wedding season. Bars and coins have drawn particular interest this Diwali.

items.headline: India's household borrowing jumps 36% as a debt-fuelled spending boom meets higher rates
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Indian household borrowing surged about 36% over the past year, raising questions over how much of the country's consumption boom is powered by debt as the Reserve Bank's rates climb. Economists warned the pace may be hard to sustain.

items.headline: Indian markets open a special Diwali session for the new Samvat trading year
items.summary: India's stock exchanges will hold a one-hour Muhurat trading session on Sunday to mark Diwali and the start of the new Hindu accounting year, Samvat. The ceremonial session, from 2:20pm to 3:30pm local time, is considered auspicious by many investors.

items.headline: Russell Brand found guilty of rape and sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court
items.summary: A London jury convicted the comedian of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, clearing him of two further rape counts and one of attempted indecent assault. The judge said a significant custodial term was inevitable and set sentencing for Monday; Brand, who denied all charges, was remanded in custody.

items.headline: PM Burnham pledges to tighten benefit eligibility for young people to curb the welfare bill
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would overhaul benefit eligibility for young people while expanding mental-health and employment support, part of a drive to rein in Britain's rising welfare bill. The plan pairs tougher eligibility rules with promises of more help into work.

items.headline: UK coverage runs short in today's edition
items.summary: BBC and Sky News were unreachable this run, and the fallback tier (Bloomberg, CNN, Al Jazeera, CNBC) yielded only two fresh UK-domestic stories after repeated retries across varied angles.

items.headline: Trump confirms fresh US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island as mediators try to avert escalation
items.summary: President Trump said US forces carried out 'minor strikes' on Iranian air defences at Qeshm Island on Friday, while claiming progress in talks. Iran said it downed a US MQ-9 drone, and a tanker caught fire after striking a mine in the Strait of Hormuz as Qatar and others pressed for de-escalation.

items.headline: Gunman kills six and wounds about 15 in a shooting in Poland's Krakow
items.summary: A gunman opened fire in Krakow's main market square on Saturday, killing six people and wounding about 15 before police shot and detained him, authorities said. Poland's interior minister said the suspect held radical far-right views.

items.headline: Death toll from a Russian strike on a Zaporizhia aid convoy rises to at least 50
items.summary: Ukrainian officials raised the death toll from a Russian strike near Zaporizhia to at least 50, up from an earlier count of 40. The attack came as Washington prepared to convene Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.

items.headline: Update: Israel's president picks Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form the next government
items.summary: President Isaac Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, rather than Benjamin Netanyahu, with forming Israel's next government, with a formal handover set for Sunday. Eisenkot, backed by parties holding 67 seats against Netanyahu's 46, has 28 days to build a coalition but has ruled out relying on Arab-led parties in cabinet.

items.headline: Binance's finance chief departs in the wake of a $6 billion crypto heist
items.summary: Binance said chief financial officer Kaiser Ng is leaving to pursue a new venture after more than five years, naming Justin Yek as his successor. The announcement came days after hackers stole more than $6 billion from the exchange; the company framed the exit as a planned transition.

items.headline: US intelligence reportedly flags a tech executive close to Nvidia's CEO as a suspected Chinese spy
items.summary: The New York Times reported that US intelligence told the Trump administration a woman close to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang - an executive at Singapore-based cloud firm Megaspeed - was recruited by a Chinese spy agency to gather information on him. Three House Republicans asked Huang to brief them; Nvidia called the interactions routine and said earlier diversion allegations were 'investigated and debunked'.

items.headline: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku
items.summary: Fox closed its roughly $22 billion takeover of Roku on Friday, ahead of a timeline that had pointed to the first half of 2027. The deal pairs Fox's live sports and news with Roku's connected-TV platform, reaching more than 100 million households, with Tubi and The Roku Channel kept separate for now.

items.headline: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production in Texas next year, Musk says
items.summary: Elon Musk said Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around the middle of next year to free capacity for the Cybercab robotaxi. Musk said he still expects Cybertrucks on the road for a long time; the angular pickup gained a niche following but never reached mass-market sales.

items.headline: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, far above forecasts
items.summary: US nonfarm payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, well above the roughly 59,000 economists expected, while the jobless rate eased to 4.1% and the prior two months were revised higher. The stronger data firmed market bets on a December Federal Reserve rate increase.

items.headline: Oil posts its worst week in months as traders weigh a renewed Iran war
items.summary: Crude settled little changed on Friday - Brent at $98.32 and WTI at $90.83 - but capped a steep weekly slide, with Brent down more than 16% and WTI off about 13%, as markets swung between hopes for an Iran deal and fears of renewed US strikes. One forecaster put the odds of fighting resuming at 80%.

items.headline: Earnings drive sharp swings: JFrog jumps about 35%, DraftKings sinks about 27%
items.summary: Software firm JFrog soared around 35% after raising its full-year guidance, while sports-betting platform DraftKings tumbled about 27% on a weak forecast, CNBC reported. The moves came as the broader market steadied after a two-day rout.

items.headline: Lam Research climbs about 9% after approving a $25 billion share buyback
items.summary: Chip-equipment maker Lam Research rose roughly 9% after its board authorised a $25 billion stock buyback, CNBC reported, among the biggest gainers in a volatile session for semiconductor shares.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris takes pole for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a rain-hit qualifying
items.summary: Lando Norris claimed pole at a wet Interlagos with a 1:27.470, beating George Russell and champion Kimi Antonelli. Russell will drop five grid places and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc 10 after penalties, reshaping the order for Sunday's race.

items.headline: 🏎️ Verstappen tops final practice but will serve a grid penalty in Brazil
items.summary: Max Verstappen set the pace in final practice at Interlagos, ahead of Antonelli and Norris, but will take a grid penalty for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix, leaving him ground to make up on race day.

items.headline: 🏏 India beat New Zealand by 4 runs in Wellington to lead the ODI series 2-0
items.summary: India held on to win a rain-shortened second ODI at Wellington by four runs on DLS, with Gurnoor Brar taking 4-30 and New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell top-scoring with 55. The result gives India a 2-0 lead in the five-match series.

items.headline: 🎾 Alcaraz and Shelton reach the Paris Masters final to set up a US Open rematch
items.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4 and Ben Shelton came back to edge Luca Van Assche 5-7, 6-3, 6-4 to reach the Rolex Paris Masters final. Sunday's title match reprises their US Open meeting.

items.headline: 🎾 Defending champion Rybakina withdraws from the WTA Finals in Indian Wells
items.summary: Elena Rybakina pulled out of the WTA Finals, which open in Indian Wells on Sunday, saying she is not physically ready to compete; Marta Kostyuk replaces her in the eight-player field. Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff headline the season-ender, staged in California after a three-year run in Riyadh.

items.headline: A new method images exoplanets up to 15 times fainter, below the telescope-stability limit
items.summary: Writing in Nature, astronomers describe a physics-based starlight-subtraction technique that uses automatic differentiation to model a telescope's own instability. Tested on JWST coronagraph data, it detected planets 4 to 15 times fainter than the standard method and edges closer to imaging Earth-like worlds.

items.headline: A brain-cell change can make silver foxes behave like pet dogs, a long fox study finds
items.summary: Researchers drawing on the 1959 Soviet silver-fox domestication experiment traced tame behaviour to a receptor protein in the ventromedial hypothalamus, a brain region tied to fear and aggression. The team now wants to know whether the same neurons shaped the temperament of dogs and wolves.

items.headline: Cannabis was burned in a Siberian burial ritual about 2,800 years ago, researchers find
items.summary: Analysis tied to a Siberian tomb pushed back evidence of ritual cannabis use to roughly 2,800 years ago, researchers reported in Science. The find adds to a picture of the plant's early ceremonial role across Central Asia.

items.headline: A self-driving lab in China writes and reads data stored in DNA from a single prompt
items.summary: Chinese researchers reported an AI-run laboratory that autonomously completed a full DNA data-storage cycle - encoding digital information into DNA and reading it back with exact recovery - with human help limited to restocking supplies. The work, published in Nature, is a step toward labs that design and run their own experiments.

fun_fact.headline: Lobster was once a poor person's food in colonial America
fun_fact.body: In colonial New England, lobster was so plentiful that it was considered a poor person's food - fed to prisoners, servants and children, and even spread on fields as fertilizer or used as fishing bait. Only in the 1800s, as railways and canning carried it inland and marketing reframed it, did lobster become the prized delicacy it is today.

puzzle.title: There and Back
puzzle.body: A cyclist rides up a long hill at a steady 10 km/h, then turns around and comes straight back down the same road at 30 km/h. What is her average speed for the whole ride? (It is not 20 km/h.)
puzzle.approach: Average speed is total distance over total time - not the average of the two speeds.
puzzle.answer: 15 km/h. Average speed = total distance / total time. For a hill of length d each way: time up = d/10, time down = d/30, total time = 2d/15 h, total distance = 2d. Average = 2d / (2d/15) = 15 km/h - the harmonic mean of 10 and 30, pulled below 20 because she spends more time crawling uphill.

word_puzzle.title: Sum of the Parts
word_puzzle.body: Unscramble each phrase into the answer described (every letter used once): 1. DIRTY ROOM -> a place to sleep (9); 2. THEY SEE -> what you see with (3,4); 3. A ROPE ENDS IT -> a feeling of hopelessness (11); 4. ELEVEN PLUS TWO -> another phrase that also equals 13 (6,4,3).
word_puzzle.approach: Rearrange all the letters of each phrase into the answer described - same letters, nothing added or dropped.
word_puzzle.answer: 1. DORMITORY; 2. THE EYES; 3. DESPERATION; 4. TWELVE PLUS ONE. Each pair uses exactly the same letters; 'eleven plus two' and 'twelve plus one' share all 13 letters and both equal 13.
